newsitem.title: UK: London Japanese stocks mixed with firmer bias.
newsitem.headline: London Japanese stocks mixed with firmer bias.

text.p: Japanese shares in London were mixed on Wednesday with buying in domestic issues and selling in blue chip stocks on currency considerations, dealers said.
The Nikkei 50 rose less than one percentage point to 1,596.52 by 1351 GMT.
"The yen is continuing to provoke buying interest in domestic-demand-led shares -- oil and construction stocks, for example - and selling in blue-chips," a dealer said.
NEC Corp lost 18.5 yen to 1,592.5 yen and Sony Corp recovered to trade 10 yen higher at 9,840 yen after a weaker London start, dealers said.
Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd shares were suspended from trade on the Tokyo bourse on Wednesday amid talk that the Japanese trust bank was planning hefty equity financing.
"This is being treated as a local market closure and we haven't been obliged to make prices, so we haven't," said one dealer.
Sumitomo closed at 1,230 yen on Tuesday ahead of the suspension.
There were also vague market rumours, later denied by the bank, that it was suffering large currency losses and may withdraw from overseas operations, traders said.
Nomura Securities Co Ltd shed 22.5 yen to 1,452.5 yen.
"People are waiting for news on the sanctions the financial authorities might take against them," said another dealer.
The giant brokerage house is under investigation over alleged payments to a racketeer, violating the Securities and Exchange Law and the Commercial Code.
